newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan subway guru says cult did not plan coup.
newsitem.headline: Japan subway guru says cult did not plan coup.

text.p: Doomsday cult guru Shoko Asahara, accused of masterminding the Tokyo subway gas attack, denied in a courtroom outburst on Friday that his sect planned to bring down the Japanese government in a coup.
"Our cult did not have any coup plans," Asahara shouted at his trial for murder during defence lawyers' cross-examination of former cult member Yoshihiro Inoue.

Inoue, once Asahara's most faithful lieutenant, served as intelligence chief of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), which police blame for the March 1995 sarin nerve gas attack which killed 12 people and made thousands ill.

Inoue, who faces his own trial for the attack, repeated previous testimony that Asahara planned the gassing to back up his mystic vision of an Armageddon end to the world that would leave the sect in power in Japan.

He said the attack was part of a master plan that included a coup takeover of Japan's military, called the Self-Defence Forces (SDF), or that would lead to a breakdown of law and order that only the sect could restore.
"That's a lie," Asahara said from his seat the dock, interrupting in a way that has become a feature of his 10-month-old trial.
"You're going to go to hell if you say such things. You should start thinking about death," Asahara said as his lawyers urged him to be silent.
Asahara has refused to enter a plea and has several times disrupted his twice-monthly trial sessions with loud outbursts that have twice led him to be evicted from the courtroom.
Apart from the subway murder charges, Asahara faces 16 other charges ranging from kidnapping to illegal production of drugs and weapons.
Asked by prosecutors if Asahara's outburst had influenced his testimony, Inoue said replied: "No, it hasn't affected my testimony. There's just a sadness which can't be put into words."
At another point in the cross-examination, Inoue was asked if he was preparing himself for a death penalty sentence in his own trial.
"I try not to think about it. I try to do what I can do now," Inoue replied after a long pause.
He also strongly denied he was shifting blame to Asahara to avoid a death penalty for himself.
